newsitem.title: UK: GUS shares slide as results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: GUS shares slide as results disappoint.

text.p: Shares in Great Universal Stores Plc tumbled on Thursday as the retail group failed to deliever a rumoured special dividend and low-end results prompted some analysts to trim earnings forecasts.
The stock, which rose to a year's high of 708p on June 13, was down 52-1/2p at 612-1/2 by 1039 GMT in moderate volume of 3.3 million.

With a number of top brokerages said to be rating the stock a "sell," analysts highlighted the cautious tone of the company's results statement -- where it said profits in the first two months of the current year were only "marginally in excess" of last year.
"In my view there is no reason to get involved until we see a turn round in the mail order side," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "At best they are a dull hold."
He said he expected to bring his current year pre-tax profit forecast back by around 10 million stg to 620 million.
"The results were without doubt a little disappointing because of the currency impact and the (poor) rate of growth in prospect," the analyst said.

GUS, which has splashed out on a series of big acquisitions in the past year including U.S. credit information services group Experian, continues to be dogged by tough trading in its core home shopping business.

GUS's underlying pre-tax profits fell to 549.1 million stg in the year ended March 31, from 562 million stg a year before. Analysts' expectations were mostly in a range of 547 million and 555 million stg.
At Williams de Broe, analyst Ian MacDougal said the stock was likely to continue under a cloud because of the lacklustre prospects for its mail order business.
"It is becoming increasingly clear that turning round the mail order business is going to be a long haul," MacDougal said.
